precepts.text: Thou shalt not revile the gods nor curse the ruler of thy people; the gods and the rulers are the same men.
precepts.point: I have said ye are gods, and all of you are children of the most High, and he meant it; but ye shall die like men, like the heathen, for the darkness we walked in, which is why we cannot afford an inferiority complex.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” Who are the gods he judges among? The law answers it: “Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people.”

The gods and the ruler of thy people are the same men. The gods are our leaders, our judges. God always moved through the leadership of our forefathers: through Moses, through Aaron, through the captains and the officers. The spirit of the Lord would move and judge us through the leaders that were acting and moving correctly in that time.

So when the psalm says he judgeth among the gods, it is referring to our leaders, the men of Israel. That is why the psalm can go on to say “all the foundations of the earth are out of course”: when our leadership walked on in darkness and Israel went into sin, the world went out of order, because its rightful heirs and rulers are not in their proper place.

And that is why the Lord could say “Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” It was not a term of endearment; he meant it. The men of the children of Israel are gods, and because of that we cannot afford low self-esteem or an inferiority complex.

precepts.text: I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the Most High.
precepts.point: After the Most High sent the flood, those same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men” in Genesis 6 is about men, not spirits; God says “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh.” Psalms 82:6 shows who these sons of God are and what God calls them: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

We are gods, and we are children of the Most High. That is why the sons of God in Genesis 6 are called by that name: they carried that DNA, made in the image of God.

It is also why their sin was so serious. Back in Genesis 6:4, “There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men.” The sons of God, the children of the Most High, took wives of the other nations, which was forbidden. The children born to them “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and “God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” So the Most High brought destruction, and later we had to pay for what we did as the sons of God; he told Abraham his seed would be afflicted in a land not theirs for four hundred years.

precepts.text: Ye are gods, children of the Most High, but ye shall die like men. We rank higher in God's creation but perish like everything else.
precepts.point: Not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think soberly. If God has revealed himself to you, humble yourself before the King of kings.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart

precepts.why:
“I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” That's why we say it: the Israelites are gods upon this earth, children of the Most High.

But read on: “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes.” We die just like men, just like the beasts of Ecclesiastes 3. In the grand scheme of things, we have no more power over death than the animals do. Are we higher up on the ladder of God's creation? Sure we are. But we perish just like everything else he has created.

That is exactly why a man must not think of himself more highly than he ought to think. Being called gods and children of the Most High is no ground for pride, because the same ones called gods fall like the princes. Think soberly: the one who knows he will die like men humbles himself before the God who made him.

precepts.text: In the kingdom the moon will shine as the sun and the sun sevenfold.
precepts.point: The prayer is for God to arise and judge the earth, for he shall inherit all nations.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” See that little g: that is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit on him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” So we walk on in gross darkness, and “all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Everything is wrong. What is out of course because of our sins? Go to Genesis: “And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night.”

Now Isaiah shows the kingdom: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days.” Does the sun have phases of transition? No. So in the kingdom the moon, which is a sign of the world, will not go back into darkness again. It is going to stay right. And the sun we say is so bright is not bright at all next to what it will be: sevenfold.

It is “in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” Binding up the breach means gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. Acts 15 quotes the prophets: “After this I will return, and will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down.” And Amos says, “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof.” Right now it is still fallen; we are trying to gather ourselves together. He will build us as in the days of old, that we may possess, own, the remnant of Edom and all the heathen.

The moon's phases started when Adam fell: the quarters, then the black moon, then it comes back. Before the fall it did not phase. That is why Israel is told, “Blow up the trumpet in the new moon, in the time appointed, on our solemn feast day”: when that brightness returns, we celebrate the Most High, because this is how it was in the beginning. When the Lord binds up the breach, the lights will be set back in course, and the moon will shine as the sun.

precepts.text: Creation waits for the manifestation of the sons of God.
precepts.point: I have said ye are gods, but ye shall die like men.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” What do we not know? “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” God judges in the congregation of the gods, and we are those beings that were with Adam in the beginning, ruling and judging this earth. That is the branches and the boughs. “But ye shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes”: it was not like that in the beginning. That is what happened after Adam fell.

Paul shows what we are waiting for: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” We have an eternal body in the heavens, the same body we had with Adam in the beginning. After Adam sinned, the Lord appointed that all of us must come on the earth through Adam in the flesh and fight to get the kingdom, the same way Christ came and overcame.

“For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” All the creatures are waiting for the sons of God to be manifest. In Genesis we are called the sons of God; we are called the twelve tribes of Israel. “Because the creature itself also shall be delivered from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of God.” We want to be delivered from this corrupted body.

Paul says of us, “even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.” We want back the body we had in the beginning, before Adam fell. To some this is foolishness; to others it is the power of God. You have to see what the Bible says. That is faith.

precepts.text: He that ascended descended first into the lower parts of the earth.
precepts.point: I have said ye are gods, but ye shall die like men.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
The children of the most High “walk on in darkness” and “die like men.” Ezra cries out over it: “it had been better not to have given the earth unto Adam: or else, when it was given him, to have restrained him from sinning.” Adam ruled the heaven and the earth. Now we live in heaviness, the nations whooping our behind, and after death look for punishment. “O thou Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee.” Adam was not the only one kicked out of paradise. All his children fell with him.

That is why Christ came and died for our sins. Through one man sin came into the world, so through one man life came. He walked perfect and died for our sins, and he will choose which of us go back with him to paradise to rule the heaven and the earth: the ones who are real, who ask forgiveness, who keep fighting and never give up.

Paul's wording shows where we came from: “Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?” Christ ascended, but first he descended. His being born on the earth is called descending. The lower parts of the earth are here in captivity, the nether parts of the earth where his sons were cast out, and they descended the same way, by being born into the earth.

Even the fathers' names show it. Jared means descend, or descent: the sons of God came down to the nether parts of the earth and died, as Adam died. And Enoch, dedicated, trained, came down, trained himself to conquer the flesh, walked perfect, “and he was not; for God took him”: he went back up to paradise.

precepts.text: Jerusalem which is above is free, the mother of us all.
precepts.point: I have said ye are gods, but ye shall die like men.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness.” We do not understand the power we have, or where we came from. Paul tells us: “But Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.”

A lot of times we read that and it goes over our heads, but pay attention to the wording. Jerusalem which is above is the mother of us all, meaning we all came from there. That is where we came from. There are different levels of understanding to these scriptures.

So when Christ says he is not of this world, and tells us we are not of this world and to love not the world, understand what he is saying. When the Bible says we are pilgrims and strangers on this earth, understand what it is saying. And when it says that if we had been mindful of whence we came, we might have had opportunity to return, understand what it is saying.

We are the sons of God cast down to the nether parts of the earth, walking in darkness and dying like men, but our mother is the Jerusalem above. You have to believe these things and understand them, because that is who you are.

precepts.text: They know not, neither will they understand; I have said, Ye are gods, and all of you are children of the Most High.
precepts.point: Acts 23 is the example: when Paul spoke against the high priest, they that stood by said, Revilest thou God's high priest? And Paul answered, I wist not, brethren, that he was the high priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people, quoting this very verse.

note.label: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not revile the gods” means do not hate or speak evil of your leaders. The word gods here is the leaders over you. The Most High says in the psalm, “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High”, speaking of us.

The psalm says of them, “They know not, neither will they understand; they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” Still they are called gods, children of the Most High, and the law says not to revile them, nor curse the ruler of thy people.

“Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.” Psalm 2 shows how the nations become an inheritance: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.”

Ask of me and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance and the uttermost parts of the earth. This goes into Christ first and foremost, and the israelites with him, receiving all nations as our inheritance and ruling over all nations. When God arises and judges the earth, the heathen are given to his Son and his people for a possession.

points: They know not, neither will they understand: neither will the people understand. All of the people walk on in darkness because the wicked is ruling; the Israelites are not ruling. I think that's the musician Asaph that wrote this, but it's still dealing with the Israelites. Like it says in Isaiah, our people are completely blind and stripped of any semblance of sanity at all.

All the foundations of the earth are out of course: out of sync, out of proper alignment. It's like driving a car and the wheels is all messed up; that car ain't going to go straight at all. That's how the earth is, cuz it's got a fool as a driver. The foundations is the very basics of everything that we do. The basics of people understanding is off. The basics of education is off. The foundation of everything that we do is corrupt.

Now it was great before, because we were in child slavery. When we were in child slavery, the prosperity, they loved it. They were just raping our women at will, doing what the hell they wanted to do with our men, our children, everything all the way up, even through the Black Wall Street era. That shows you the resistance that we had to even persevere. And Black Wall Street was not the only place: there were towns all over this country that we controlled. Durham, North Carolina was another one; even Central Park, we had control over a section of that; Rosewood, all those areas. In defiance of this virulent hatred that this beast did upon us, we were still able to stand and still do things for ourselves. That's in the 20s coming up.

Now we move up to the 50s and the 60s: the Jim Crow laws, the black codes, convict leasing. Could you imagine the turbulent times? As we're sitting in here, the times would be like you go outside and you might get lynched; just imagine that as an everyday reality. We forget these things; we done got comfortable. You could not really go out anywhere and experience any kind of dignity as a man. White man come kick you on your behind while you're walking, and you couldn't really do nothing, because he got the whole police force behind him, the government behind him, all of the doctors, because all of it was segregated. There was no oversight for the ugliness that they would do to us systemwide.

Quote read in class: when FBI director J. Edgar Hoover was asked what in his opinion was the single greatest threat to the United States of America, he responded: negro unity. So they said, we cannot have negroes being unified, because that would disrupt the unity that we already have to keep them permanently oppressed. Who was Hoover against? The people of the civil rights era, the Panthers, Dr. Martin Luther King, Medgar Evers; all those people represented unity. And I'm only speaking about the southern kingdom; he had this thing with the Young Lords, all of the other tribes. The whole point of the unity is that this bond of white supremacy must continue, even if we have to change the name of the few that runs it.

You hear people talk about, man, it's a system that keep us down. The system is made of men. But the point is there is a unified organized force that kept us in chains, that kept us segregated, that kept us discriminated, that kept us from any kind of opportunity to do any upward mobility for your community. There was literal legal systems that kept us out of any kind of prosperity. Could you imagine living under that psychological tyranny every day? Like Malcolm said, you walking down the street and some cracker put his hands on your woman and you not supposed to be emotional. He said, you ain't supposed to get upset. Because it was like that.

Charles Drew, the doctor that invented blood plasma, the blood bank: his name should be on all the banks. He was in a terrible car accident; he needed blood and they refused him. They refused him service to give him blood, and his own damn invention is in the damn hospital. And then they tried to lie, say, no, that ain't it. That is what happened. That's the kind of tyranny we lived under.

When we came up in this truth, we had a camp sign that said Dr. Martin Luther King is in the Bible, and we would read Jeremiah 23:25, I have dreamed, I have dreamed, and it was talking about false prophets. I understand the reason why we would do it, because you got to get people's attention; our job is to compel people. But some will look at that and will be calling Dr. Martin Luther King an Uncle Tom, calling certain people that was getting completely abused out here trying to go against the very terrible system of what I just spoke about. A lot of people talk in ignorance; don't really understand what it was like to live in those terrible times. Man can't even get up early in the morning, but yet he gonna talk smack about what those men were doing. The elders, they knew about this; they were grown men when all this went down.

News read in class: James Meredith is best known for integrating the University of Mississippi, Ole Miss, in 1962. His courageous enrollment forced the federal government to intervene against state resistance. Later, his 1966 March Against Fear catalyzed a massive voter registration drive for black Americans across the south.

Could you imagine the type of organizing or strategy effort that it took to at least win some of them to be quote unquote on our side, to allow this man who was well overqualified to go to this university? When there's none of us in there, there's no oversight for them to do to you what they do. You might feel a little comfortable if you get pulled over and there might be a black man in the passenger seat, but you have no idea what that police officer is dealing when they go back to the precinct, because he's probably the only spot in there. They're going to put a possum on your locker, all kind of things. Brothers had to go through this kind of stuff. But it was strategy to try to get our people on the other side within the power structure to somewhat offset the evils that all of these agencies were doing to us. Number one, it is of the Lord 100 percent; there's nobody questioning that. But I'm just giving you the byproducts by which the Lord moved to make things happen. Don't get me wrong, the Bible ain't about no integration. But in their mind at that time, that's all they knew.

Story told in class: around the early 70s, black people driving in a nice convertible; he was from North Carolina, telling the people in Philadelphia about the virulent racism that black people dealt with in the south. While they were driving, a white cop pulled him over and said, listen, follow me; another police car got behind the convertible to make sure that he don't dip to the left or to the right. They pull up to a working class white neighborhood. The cop goes and gets the white woman out the house; she comes out crying like she was just raped. The cop brings the woman over to the brothers sitting in the car and said, are these the guys? The white woman said, no. The cop said, are you sure? She said, no, they're not the guys. The cop said, okay, y'all get out of here. One of the passengers said, by the way, could you tell us what you pull us over for? The guy said, man, the hell with that, let's get the hell out of here. They jumped in the damn car, ran through red lights and everything. But the white cop said, listen, I told y'all to get out of here before I change my mind. And that was everyday life.

Me and Deacon Asaph used to work together in a hospital in Manhattan, and there was a librarian, very old woman, and she used to tell us lots of stories just like this. She was telling us stories about how they would put black men in jail and allow the lynch mob to come in and take them out the jail and kill them in the middle of the street.

The turbulence and the ugliness of what was going on in those times dictated a certain level of strategy that people today can't even understand. And sometimes we are so loose with our mouths, loose with our thoughts, and you go speaking against something, and many of our people today don't even have enough discipline to even know how to use the bathroom, and they talking smack.

This country is about taking things back to the quote unquote good old days. And the good old days for them is the bad old days for us. This eighth head has the attributes of all the rest of the seven, and they set themselves up as the imperial of all the rest of them. So they all honor and worship this beast America, mainly because they have the greatest concentration of its labor, meaning us. That's what made it great. They recognized that in order for it to remain great, we have to continue to keep the process of slavery going by another name. They want the blood of your sons and daughters so that they can continue to make America great again the way they had it once, when we was in total domination and total destruction.

Imagine that: you're on a slave plantation, you get married to your woman, you jump over a broom. Him and the wife was sleeping in the slave quarters, and the so-called master comes up from another plantation: what you got down there in the quarters? I'm looking for something tasty tonight. And the white man would take the man's wife out the bed and defile the hell out of her, and then send her back to him soiled, used. And before he takes her away from him, he turns to the husband and said, don't worry, when she returns to you, she'll be more worthy. These things happen. And then she has to come back to the man that was unable to protect her, and she still had to find a way to make him feel like a man, knowing that he couldn't protect her. Imagine that kind of psychology. We today, we are detached from those kinds of things. We got to take this truth more serious, cuz this ain't no game out here. What's about to go down in this system, our people going to catch hell. Northern kingdom, southern kingdom, all the tribes going to catch hell.

They're doing the gerrymandering with the seats, changing the voting districts; all that means getting blacks out of power. And once you're not in certain seats where you can oversee the wicked actions of those that have control over you, they will run with free reign to do whatever they want to do. How is it that Rasheen Carter can't get any justice in Taylorsville, Mississippi? Cuz there ain't no conscious blacks down there overseeing anything. My sister Tiffany Carter, her heart is heavy every day, trying to get justice, when that grief is still there, knowing that our son was butcherly mutilated. You also have Kendrick Johnson: his organs missing, and they had the temerity to tell us that he climbed into a rolled up mat reaching for a shoe, but meanwhile his arms is to his side. But they can say that when there's no consequence.

These children were juveniles in their mind; they were not aware of the consequences of their actions because those actions and their behavior were not daunted with fear. That's a biblical word, by the way; it's in the Bible.

Bishop was talking about the barbershop crew in Brooklyn: they were working out so that they could have the confidence to rob houses, ripping doors open, busting in and stealing. They obviously were not daunted with fear. That's what's happening to a lot of these young kids: they pushed past the inhibitions that parents may have given to them, that community leaders might have given to them, that says, sisters don't do that, brothers don't do this. That's the reason why the Lord gave you that inhibition, that fear. But if you're influenced to go beyond that and your prefrontal cortex have not properly developed, you will think that you're doing something that is no consequence. But the next thing you know, you're doing life in prison before you're even 20 years old. And the state love that, because that's that sweat equity that we want out of him.

They have no empathy. They don't care about how many people that got ripped apart by the bullets that they shot out of those weapons. Don't care how many grieving families is going to be the result of all that carnage. A disregard for social norms, mainly the Bible, a disregard for the laws, the rules: the hell with mama, the hell with daddy, the hell with the teachers, the hell with the community leaders. I'm gonna do my own thing and end up sweat equity or dead.

Image shown: the four defendants plus the girl charged with the murder of Julio Foolio, Charles Jones. All of these guys were under the age of about 20, 21. Every last one of them got life without parole except the girl. They will never see the outside of a jail cell again. They will only leave the prison in a body bag with a number attached to it. Their name is gone; when that gavel swung and dropped, their name disappeared. They became a number, property of the state. And they made that decision at 20 years old. Why? Because of some drill rap crap.

Alicia Maya got 15 years because she wasn't quote unquote active in the killings; she was a getaway driver basically. So she'd be like in her mid 40s by the time she even get out. Her life is pretty much ruined. And I heard a guy talking about the case on YouTube saying, yo, she's a little baddie.

Confident to do 15 years. Highly stylish to do 15 years. This is what you get when your prefrontal cortex is not developed and you following stupidity. This whole system is set up to drive our people just like this. Why do you think they are against what we're doing? We're trying to save our kids from becoming this, trying to save the young sisters and the young brothers from becoming sweat equity. That's the reason why they hate us so much: because we're getting in their way. This is the unity; J. Edgar Hoover, even his old racist red ass is dead, the mentality is still out here all over the place.
